office_does: A Mason PUD 3 commissioner sits on the three-member elected board that sets policy, the budget and rates for the public electric and fiber utility serving most of Mason County, for a six-year term; the whole PUD votes.
race_blurb: Open seat: Commissioner Tom Farmer is not on the ballot. Sitting county commissioner Randy Neatherlin runs on 20 years in local office and a goal of no rate increases for four years. Retired state land surveyor and Forest Festival president Mick Sprouffske praises PUD 3's public power and fiber service and pledges affordable rates within state mandates.

candidates.summary: Licensed land surveyor retired from the state Department of Natural Resources, Navy veteran and Mason County Forest Festival president, running for his first elected office.
highlights: Managed DNR's Public Land Survey Office, working with all 39 county auditors [S1]
Credits PUD 3's public power with lower rates, reliability and shorter outages, and praises its fiber program [S1]
Will advocate for affordable electricity rates 'as allowed by state mandates' [S1]

candidates.summary: Mason County Commissioner (District 1) in his fourth term and former Port of Allyn commissioner, running on rate restraint and broadband.
highlights: 14 years as county commissioner and 6 as a Port of Allyn commissioner [S1][S3]
Aims for zero rate increases for four years by 'budgeting and living within our means' [S1]
Prioritizes PUD broadband competition, local service hubs and infrastructure for future growth [S1]
